```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# reserves blank work space (no ruled lines); pair with fig.height
blank_space <- function() {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
}
```

**NRES 746, Week 11, Lecture 2: Two Cores from One Tree**

Name: ___________________________________________

**Instructions:** Work alone on Part 1 (about 4 minutes), then work
with a neighbor on Part 2. Keep laptops closed.

You want the mean annual ring width of the pinyon pines in a stand. Each
increment core gives one measurement $X$ with variance
$\sigma^2 = 0.04$ mm$^2$ ($\sigma = 0.2$ mm). Two facts you'll need:

$$\text{Var}(aX) = a^2\,\text{Var}(X) \qquad
\text{Var}(X + Y) = \text{Var}(X) + \text{Var}(Y) + 2\,\text{Cov}(X, Y)$$

where $\text{Cov}(X, Y) = \rho\,\sigma_X\sigma_Y$ and $\rho$ is the
correlation between $X$ and $Y$.

## Part 1: Two cores (individual)

You average two cores, $M = (X_1 + X_2)/2$.

**1a.** If the two cores come from different trees ($\rho = 0$),
$\text{Var}(M) =$ ____________ mm$^2$.

**1b.** If both cores come from the same tree ($\rho = 0.6$),
$\text{Var}(M) =$ ____________ mm$^2$.

```{r fig.height=0.3*6}
blank_space()
```

## Part 2: Ten cores (with a neighbor)

**2a.** Design A: ten cores from one tree (every pair has $\rho = 0.8$).
Design B: one core from each of ten trees (independent). Which design
estimates the stand's mean more precisely, and by how much? Ten cores
from one tree are worth about how many independent cores?

More precise: Design ______, by a factor of about ______. Ten cores from
one tree $\approx$ ______ independent cores.

```{r fig.height=0.3*9}
blank_space()
```
